source_text.Q-1042: MEDIUM, owner CI lane (follow-up of Q-1037, the next lever after sharding). Reported by the supervisor 2026-10-08. Evidence: ExUnit reports ~0.5 s average per test and ~66 min of cumulative test work per backend run (7.7k tests); a large share is believed to be the per-test tenant schema clone from tenant_template (CREATE SCHEMA ... LIKE tenant_template... for every table, see the LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE setup/teardown log lines and the 'tenant_template_build' schemas): cost per test = DDL for every table of the template plus DROP SCHEMA CASCADE at teardown. NOT yet measured: step 1 is to instrument (time per clone, number of tables cloned, share of test time) on one partition, step 2 choose the lever: (a) clone only the tables the test needs, (b) share a read-only tenant across tests that do not mutate it (async-safe), (c) a pooled tenant per module with truncate-reset, (d) Postgres schema cloning via CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE or a faster mechanism; keep isolation guarantees (no cross-test leakage, the ISS-0410-class isolation bugs). Each step measured before/after; mutation proof that isolation still holds (a test that leaves data behind must not leak into the next). Overlap check 2026-10-08: Q-1037 is the umbrella; ISS-0410 (isolation failure, blocked) is background, not a duplicate.

task.description:
WF-03 Step 4 (regression/isolation test design) for ISS-1042 / Q-1042, = WF-02 Step 3. You are TEST-DESIGNER. Role file .claude/agents/test-designer.md.

WHAT TO WRITE: test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs (ExUnit; async: false) that proves the pooled tenant fixture's isolation guarantees, plus a spec file test/specs/ISS-1042.md (why each test exists, mapped to the acceptance criteria). Spec of record: lib/letflow/design/iss1042-pooled-tenant-fixture.md section 9 (isolation proof / mutation classes M1..M22 (the list may be M1..M21 + variants: use the design's own enumeration, do not invent classes)). Implementation under test: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (Letflow.TenantFixture pool API) and test/support/tenant_template.ex. The implementer left hooks for you: pool_opts parity_check: true, pool_end_fence!/0, pool_stats/1 generations, after_verify/after_guard hooks (they RUN IN THE WORKER; per-test claim state is in the TEST PROCESS dictionary: read implementer notes below).

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Every design mutation class gets at least one test that FAILS if the guarantee is violated: leave-behind rows incl. FK chains; sequence advanced with row gone; seed-table modification; public keyed rows (secrets, event_history_retirement_outcomes and catalog-discovered tables); tenants/registration row changes; committed structure drift with unchanged counts (DISABLE TRIGGER, column/index/constraint/sequence/comment/function alteration); late writer after verify and after the final guard; lock timeout; straggler idle-in-transaction; async module rejection; misordered attach_pool! (REVIEWER R3: also assert the misorder rejection still FIRES, because the owning_module/0 and test_process?/0 rescues would silently disable it if ExUnit internals change); undeclared shape; teardown with no provisioned tenant (Sandbox.mode(:auto) ownership); first-acquire verification; rebuild path refreshes registration snapshot and generation; default (non-pool) path unchanged for template: :replay and teardown: false. Order-independence: each leak test is a pair of tests whose cross-test visibility is checked deterministically (use a test-boundary simulation via recycle_pool!/pool_end_fence! as the design says, not reliance on ExUnit's random order).
2. Property/data-driven where the design says so (StreamData is available); do not over-generate: the suite must stay fast (target < 120 s wall for the file; a pooled module is the point of this issue).
3. FAIL-FIRST PROOF (WF-03 'code under test does not exist' rule, WF-03_issue_resolving.md section 'When the pre-fix failure is non-existence'): you must MUTATE the shipped logic and record, per mutant, which tests fail. Mutants must target the specific traps (e.g. digest ignores tgenabled; reset truncates only direct-dirty tables without FK closure; sequences not reset; seed not restored; final guard removed; verify skipped on first acquire; rebuild does not re-snapshot registration; Sandbox.mode(:auto) removed from teardown; async rejection removed). Aim for at least 12 mutants covering distinct classes; each must be killed by at least one test, and record any survivor honestly with the reason. Apply mutants ONLY in a throwaway `git worktree` of the branch (preferred), or revert with `git checkout -- <path>` and verify `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` is empty and the file re-runs green; leaving a mutant in the tree is a step failure. A mutant table (mutant, file/line, tests failed N/M) goes in result.summary and test/specs/ISS-1042.md.
4. Environment: a Postgres is NOT guaranteed running. Use a throwaway docker container on its own port (see how handoffs/WF03-ISS1042-20261012/step-03-elixir-dev.json result.summary and docs/anti-patterns.md ran theirs, port 5499 was used); stop and remove any container you start; leave no schemas or scratch files. Quote real command output: the file run (N tests, 0 failures, wall time), run twice for flake check, plus `mix format --check-formatted` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`.
5. Do not edit test/support/* or any adopter module (that is implementation; if a test cannot be written without a seam, report it as an issue in the handoff). Do not touch CI files.
6. Commit tests and spec to the branch in small commits tagged [Q-1042 / GH #2381] and push. Complete the handoff per docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md (artifacts_out lists files; next_action 'Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR'). Do not edit handoffs/registry.json or handoffs/orchestrator.log.

REVIEWER NOTES (non-blocking, already accepted):
- [MINOR] Follow-up: adopt security F2 - assert current_database() starts with letflow_test (the configured test database) in start_pool!/2 or Pool.init before any DDL. Non-blocking.
- [MINOR] parity_check: opt, pool_end_fence!/0 and pool_stats.generations have no caller outside the pool code yet; keep only if TEST-DESIGNER consumes them at step 4, otherwise remove (scope creep).
- [MINOR] owning_module/0 and test_process?/0 rescue-all to nil/false: a future ExUnit internals change would silently disable the misordered-attach rejection (falls back to per-test clone, slower not unsafe). TEST-DESIGNER should include a test that the rejection still fires.
- [MINOR] Docs: docs/anti-patterns.md item 2 and ISS-1042.yaml server_side_microbenchmarks say TRUNCATE of "all 57 tables of a clone"; a clone has 50 plain tables, 57 is the template incl. partitions. Correct at DOC-UPDATER step.
- [INFO] Type-safety observation (does not block): worker state, slot records and the process-dictionary claim map are untyped plain maps with atom statuses; a @type or small struct for slot/state would make a missing :baseline or invalid status unrepresentable rather than caught by probes/tests. Role file says to file this under docs/issues tagged type-safety; NOT filed by me because this dispatch limits REVIEWER to editing only its own handoff - ORCH please file it (low priority, test infrastructure).
- [INFO] Implementer deviations from design 3.2/3.4 (unlinked start, tenant_snapshot not re-taken on rebuild, FK graph recomputed per reset) judged sound; design text should be updated by CODE-DESIGNER/DOC-UPDATER if the doc is kept.

IMPLEMENTER NOTE FOR YOU:
For TEST-DESIGNER / TEST-RUNNER: (1) the per-test claim state lives in the test process dictionary, hooks (after_verify / after_guard) run in the worker so a test must drive them through a global (persistent_term/atomics), as my throwaway probe did; (2) fence A and the end fence only fire for an in-flight client backend whose query text contains the slot schema or tenant id, M14 therefore needs an INSERT (schema is in the first bytes); (3) log lines to count for the 5+5 table: phase=pool_clone, phase=pool_acquire outcome=clean|reset|rebuilt, phase=pool_reset, phase=pool_fallback; check outcome counts, not just wall time (see the anti-pattern entry).
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented measurement: clone time per test, tables per clone, share of total test time (numbers quoted)
One lever implemented with before/after wall time of the test phase (5 runs each, run ids)
Isolation proof: a test leaving data behind does not leak into the next test (mutation test)
No change to required check names; no paid runners

Wrote test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs (4 modules, 57 tests = 56 tests + 1 StreamData property) and test/specs/ISS-1042.md. Covers design 9.3 M1..M7, M8a/b, M9, M10, M11, M12, M13a/b/c, M14, M15..M21 (15 data-driven definition mutations incl. DISABLE TRIGGER ALL on internal RI triggers, OWNED BY NONE, MATCH FULL), M22 (double attach, undeclared shape, async/missing-async/empty/unknown-key/duplicate pool), a separate pooled module with NO attach (REVIEWER R3: the misorder rejection still FIRES), a first-acquire module (F5/INV-P12), a teardown module with no provisioned tenant and Sandbox left {:shared, dead} (F6), catalog discovery of keyed public tables compared with an independent formulation, rebuild refreshes Registration snapshot/generation, seed re-copy that cannot reproduce the baseline fails verify. Hooks, parity_check, pool_end_fence!/0 and pool_stats.generations are all consumed (answers the REVIEWER scope-creep note). Every mutation test asserts the pool's report SEES the mutation (teeth) and the pristine check uses independent direct reads, not only the pool's own probe; after resets/rebuilds assert_clone_parity! (13 dims) is the independent oracle.

Result: 57 passed (1 property, 56 tests)'.
